details: Found by the front 30 Oct ~06:20Z: right after `relay queue start one-digest-per-wave-instead-of-status-messages`, before its worker's first commit, the lanes hook said 'landed, still open: one-digest-per-wave-instead-of-status-messages (wt/one-digest-per-wave-instead-of-status-me landed)', told the front to close it by hand with `relay queue done --evidence`, and counted 5 of 6 lanes running while 6 were busy, offering a start that would overfill the lanes. A branch whose head equals the default branch's (nothing committed yet) is read as merged.
failing_case: Take an item with `relay queue start`; before any commit on its branch, lanes_state lists it under landed_open and not under running.
pass_cases: A taken item with a fresh branch at the default branch's head is running, not landed
A branch merged into the default branch with the item closed there is not running
A branch merged with the item still open on the default branch is landed_open
findings.summary: A just-started branch with no commit counts as landed

details: CONFIRMED (scratch repo, output in evidence). The change found the real parsing gap (git appends " (no commit created; -m option ignored)"
to a fast-forward reflog entry when -m is given, so `subject.endswith("Fast-forward")` misses it) but fixed it in a new function
relay_lane_features.own_commits used only by landing(). relay_git.has_own_commits, "shared" since 4e38f266 precisely so every program
reads own commits the same way, is unchanged and still used by relay_lanes._one_lane_per_train (line 267), relay_tidy.lines (line 41),
and the merge hook's clean (line 81), riders (line 439) and removable (line 567). Two definitions of one fact now disagree; the callers the
change did not update keep the wrong answer, and in the merge hook that wrong answer removes a worktree. Project rule (CLAUDE.local.md,
Python): one parser shared by all programs that read a record. Fixing has_own_commits in place also removes the need for the 600-line move.
evidence: merge master: Fast-forward (no commit created; -m option ignored)
failing_case: Repo with master; `git worktree add -b wt/x ../x`; a commit on master; in ../x `git merge -m take master`.
Reflog of wt/x: "merge master: Fast-forward (no commit created; -m option ignored)", "branch: Created from HEAD".
Now: relay_git.has_own_commits(repo, "wt/x") -> True while relay_lane_features.own_commits -> False;
relay_tidy.lines(repo) -> [(True, "merged worktree still present: ../x (wt/x)")] (doctor offers to remove a lane that has not started);
plugins/relay/hooks/merge.py clean()/removable()/riders() pass guard 3 and may remove wt/x and its worktree after the next merge.
Should: has_own_commits -> False; tidy lists nothing for wt/x; the merge hook keeps wt/x ("it has no commits of its own").
fix_hint: Put the corrected test in relay_git.has_own_commits (skip subjects that start with "branch: Created from" or "reset: moving to", or that
start with "merge " and contain ": Fast-forward"), drop relay_lane_features.own_commits and call relay_git.has_own_commits in landing again;
add a test for relay_git.has_own_commits (or relay_tidy.lines) with the -m reflog entry.
pass_cases: 1. The failing case: relay_git.has_own_commits -> False and relay_tidy.lines lists no "merged worktree" line for wt/x.
2. Fresh branch with only "branch: Created from refs/heads/master" and "merge master: Fast-forward" (relay queue start's own path) -> False.
3. A branch with one real commit, then fast-forwarded into master -> True; tidy lists it as a merged worktree; lanes_state lists it landed_open while its item is open.
4. test_fresh_branch_that_took_master_with_a_message_is_running_not_landed still passes with landing calling the single shared function.
reason: lib/relay_git.py:508 one has_own_commits; test_has_own_commits_ignores_a_fast_forward_taken_with_a_message_and_tidy_lists_nothing passes, fails on base.
findings.summary: the -m fast-forward fix lives in a second copy (own_commits); relay_git.has_own_commits keeps the bug, so relay doctor and the merge hook still treat a fresh worktree that took master with -m as merged with own work

details: CONFIRMED by reading: `"Fast-forward" in s` matches anywhere in the subject, including a "commit: <message>" entry. Anchor it to merge entries
(s.startswith("merge ") and ": Fast-forward" in s). Rare today, hence LOW; cheap to fix together with F1. Size: 5 minutes.
failing_case: Fresh wt/x; one commit with message "docs: explain Fast-forward merges" (reflog "commit: docs: explain Fast-forward merges"); fast-forward
master to it while the item is still open. Now: own_commits -> False, landing -> (False, None), the item stays "running" instead of landed_open.
Should: own_commits -> True, the item is listed landed_open.
fix_hint: Match only merge entries: `s.startswith("merge ") and ": Fast-forward" in s`.
pass_cases: 1. Reflog "commit: docs: explain Fast-forward merges" + "branch: Created from refs/heads/master" -> own commits True.
3. "merge master: Fast-forward (no commit created; -m option ignored)" -> skipped.
reason: Anchored to "merge " entries (lib/relay_git.py:508); test_commit_message_mentioning_fast_forward_is_an_own_commit_and_lands passes (also on base, as own_commits was the buggy copy and is removed).
findings.summary: own_commits skips any reflog entry containing "Fast-forward", so a branch whose only own commit has that word in its subject counts as having none
